feedback: Written before this robot has raced, and there are no further iterations after this one, so this feedback is advisory only. The geometry is held at the iteration 5 reference, which is the best-evidenced layout (score 422.9, oval finish 95%). Iteration 10 (seven sensors at 12 mm pitch) scored 331.2 and did not reduce slalom line losses, so denser sensing is not supported. Iteration 9 (radius 0.045 m) fell to 389.9, and iteration 8 (outer spread 0.045 m) fell to 309.4. Iteration 6 (mass 0.4 kg) and iteration 7 (track 0.09 m) also lowered the score, so no single-variable geometry change has beaten iteration 5. I made no controller change, since none has been measured on this body. The known weak points, s-bend off-track at max_error near 0.06 m and slalom line losses near 1.85, are for the controller side to address, and a geometry change would be an untested gamble on the final race. If the Integrator reports that s-bend or slalom off-track exits dominate, that points to line-loss handling and gain choice, not sensing, so the geometry should stay as it is.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration 5 geometry exactly (five sensors at y=0.07 m, x = -0.036 to 0.036 m, 16 mm footprints, track 0.10 m, radius 0.040 m, mass 0.5 kg). Iterations 6 to 10 each lowered the score from this reference, and the final race is scored once.

If any future development result were available, test only one variable at a time against iteration 5, for example sensor y at 0.06 m with the same spread, since iteration 3 showed that y=0.08 m raised oscillation and cut the oval finish rate.
Do not widen the outer spread beyond 0.036 m or change the track or radius without evidence, since iterations 7, 8 and 9 each cost oval finish rate.
